Final 3 seconds (5-8s): the glyph 秒 is perfectly still and fully readable while the lead keeps a small joyful motion away from the strokes. Bright but not neon palette, no watermark, no flashing, no other writing.

conceptZh: 橡膠恐龍想按碼錶上的小紅鈕，小手搆不到就用全身衝刺，結果飛過按鈕撞倒一疊藍色橡膠長條，長條落下排成「秒」，牠冒煙滑回來輕輕用大腳趾一點，秒針就滴答轉動。
object: a chunky toy stopwatch with a tiny red start button, plus a tall leaning stack of nine blue rubber rods
morph: the dinosaur's overshoot crash knocks the nine rubber rods into the air; five fall on the left as 禾 (slant, bar, upright, two splaying legs) and four on the right as 少 (upright, two dots, long sweeping slant), locking into a clean 秒
creativeAngle: 沿用「力氣太大」模式但換成全新主角與道具：上一版是玩具戰士用泡棉劍彈球、三秒鐘；這版是橡膠恐龍小手搆不到按鈕，用全身衝過頭，撞散的橡膠長條直接落成字，最後輕輕一點腳趾就成功，並改用「秒針」一詞，讓聽到的詞與畫面上轉動的秒針同時出現。
promptEn:
An 8-second 3D cartoon clip on a pale buttercup-yellow background. The only text ever on screen is the single Traditional Chinese glyph 秒, in thick solid cobalt-blue strokes, centered, uncropped, about 70% of frame height with clean margins.

Lead: a squishy mint-green rubber dinosaur with enormous flat feet and two comically tiny arms that cannot reach anything. Prop: a chunky orange toy stopwatch standing on the floor at center-right, with one tiny red start button on top. Behind it, a tall neat stack of nine blue rubber rods leans against the right edge. Nothing else in the scene.

0-1.5s: The dinosaur stares at the tiny red button, leans in and strains both tiny arms toward it, missing by a mile, belly pressed against the stopwatch. It huffs, then backs up to the far left edge, digs its huge feet into the floor and revs up like a sprinter, eyes narrowed on the button.

1.5-3.2s: The first 秒 is spoken as it launches. The dinosaur thunders across the frame left to right, leaps belly-first at the button, sails clean over it, and crashes with a big rubbery BONK into the stack of blue rods. Squash-and-stretch on impact, the stack bursts upward, rods spinning in the air.

3.2-5s: The dinosaur skids backward on smoking feet to the center of the floor and stops with a wobble and a dizzy cross-eyed grin. The nine rods rain down above it and click into place one after another: five on the left form 禾 (a short slant, a horizontal bar, a tall upright, two splaying legs), four on the right form 少 (an upright, a dot on each side, a long sweeping slant). The second 秒 is spoken exactly as the last rod snaps in and the glyph 秒 locks solid. The stopwatch has bounced to the bottom-right corner, small and clear of the strokes.

5-8s: The glyph 秒 holds perfectly still and fully readable. Below it, the dinosaur tiptoes to the little stopwatch and, with great care, taps the red button with one giant toe. The stopwatch springs alive and its red second hand sweeps a clear ticking arc. The word 秒針 is spoken exactly as that second hand starts moving. The dinosaur does a tiny proud stomp-dance in the bottom corner, never touching or covering the strokes.

Audio: a warm, friendly off-screen voice in clear Taiwanese Mandarin reads exactly "秒、秒、秒針" (ㄇㄧㄠˇ、ㄇㄧㄠˇ、ㄇㄧㄠˇ ㄓㄣ), slowly and distinctly with clear tones, a short pause between the two single utterances, and stops after the word. Soft rubbery boings and one light tick, quieter than the voice. No other speech, no subtitles, no vocabulary text, no watermark, no flashing. Bright but not neon colors, no white blowouts, no dark grading.
